To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the WEA service is effective and efficient in emergency situations that can be addressed by a short text message, (2) it can be improved through the addition of a location-based service, (3) it can be enhanced through the use of maps, (4) it can be augmented through the provision of a digest of the alert information, and (5) it can be made more effective by the addition of a mechanism for users to report the receipt of the alert.

the WEA service needs to be improved in the following areas: (1) geo-targeting augmented by location information and maps, (2) digested presentation of information, (3) user control over the alerts they receive, (4) the ability to provide feedback to alert originators, and (5) the ability to receive alerts from sources other than the federal government and state and local governments.
the WEA service is effective and efficient for delivering short, simple, and unchanging text messages, but the service needs improvements in order to deliver more complex and dynamic information.

improving the effectiveness of the WEA service through better contextualization and presentation of information.
improving the WEA service to make it more effective in delivering information that is vital and actionable.
the design and evaluation of extensions to WEA that can enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of emergency alerts.

the WEA service is a valuable tool for alert originators and wireless subscribers, but the service can be significantly improved to better support the delivery of information to wireless subscribers.
